boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Northwest University spaces for studying, gathering, making, performing, and recreation, supported by current university pages.

cards.title: H-214 24-Hour Study Space
cards.subtitle: D.V. Hurst Library
cards.notes: Use the key-card study room when you need computers, tables, a printer, and a focused place to continue work beyond library desk hours.
cards.short_summary: A key-card-access study room with computers and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: NU identifies H-214 as a 24-hour study space with seating, tables, computers, and a printer; NU ID key card is required.
cards.access_notes: Typically open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for student study needs; NU ID key card required. Check the library page for closure exceptions.

cards.title: Hurst Library Upper-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: D.V. Hurst Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a project meeting, then close the door for conversation-level work without disrupting the library’s designated quiet upper level.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms sized for individual pairs and small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: The library has three large and four small upper-floor study rooms; large rooms serve groups of 2–6 and small rooms 1–2, with reservations available to NU students.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are recommended and have priority; NU students, faculty, and staff may reserve for up to two hours daily.

cards.title: Hurst Library 1st Floor Seating Area
cards.subtitle: D.V. Hurst Library
cards.notes: Choose this ground-floor library stop for an easy transition between the building entrance, the nearby study room, and your next campus errand.
cards.short_summary: First-floor seating beside Hurst Library’s 24-hour study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwest University’s campus-tour page places the 24-hour computer-lab study room by the Hurst Library first-floor seating area.
cards.source_title: Hurst Library 1st Floor Seating Area | Northwest University
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours vary by term; consult the library hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Pecota Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student lounge, commuter lounge, and campus offices
cards.notes: Meet a friend between classes, use the commuter lounge for lunch, or plan a club gathering in the building’s shared student-centered spaces.
cards.short_summary: A central student hub for hanging out, studying, lunch, and club meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: NU describes Pecota as a student hub with space for studying, friends, commuter community and lunch, plus meetings for clubs and organizations.
cards.access_notes: The building also houses Student Development and Campus Ministries offices; office availability may vary.

cards.title: The Green
cards.subtitle: Northwest University campus lawn
cards.notes: Bring a few classmates outside for casual recreation; student equipment rentals can support soccer, volleyball, or spikeball on the lawn.
cards.short_summary: Campus green space paired with student recreation equipment rentals.
cards.evidence_claim: NU’s campus-tour transcript says students use The Green to hang out and can rent soccer, volleyball, and spikeball equipment from SAB.
cards.access_notes: Use equipment through SAB according to its current rental process; outdoor conditions and scheduled events may affect use.

cards.title: Kristi Brodin Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Campus gymnasium
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for an intramural game, student event, or varsity contest when you want an indoor group activity or a place to cheer.
cards.short_summary: The campus gym hosts sports, intramurals, and student events.
cards.evidence_claim: NU’s campus-tour transcript identifies the Pavilion as a site for sporting events, Screaming Eagles Week, and intramural games.
cards.access_notes: Event access and schedules vary; confirm the current athletic or campus-events schedule before attending.

cards.title: Millard Theatre
cards.subtitle: Millard Hall
cards.notes: Look for a drama performance, recital, or scheduled Improv gathering here when you want to experience a campus performance with other students.
cards.short_summary: A campus performance venue inside Millard Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: NU states that Millard Theatre is equipped for performances, plays, and recitals; its campus-tour transcript says the drama department stages plays in Millard.
cards.access_notes: Attend scheduled university events; access outside event times may be restricted.

cards.title: Butterfield Chapel
cards.subtitle: Chapel auditorium and Amundsen Music Center rooms
cards.notes: Attend a scheduled chapel service or student performance, and use the posted event calendar to find gatherings that fit your academic schedule.
cards.short_summary: A chapel-service and performance setting overlooking the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2025–26 undergraduate catalog says Butterfield Chapel is the setting for university chapel services and contains Amundsen Music Center classrooms, rehearsal rooms, studios, and practice rooms.
cards.access_notes: Use for scheduled chapel services, performances, or approved events; confirm individual event access and times.

cards.title: Argue Health and Sciences Center
cards.subtitle: Science labs, classrooms, and student academic gatherings
cards.notes: Use this academic building as a meeting point around science classes, then follow department directions for access to classrooms and laboratories.
cards.short_summary: A health-and-sciences academic building with labs and classrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: NU’s catalog states that Argue Health and Science Center contains science laboratories for chemistry, physical science, mathematics, geology, and biological sciences.
cards.access_notes: Academic rooms and laboratories may require class enrollment, supervision, or department permission.

cards.title: Eagle Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness facility
cards.notes: Plan a workout with a classmate and check with campus staff for current access rules, equipment availability, and any facility closures.
cards.short_summary: A student-and-faculty fitness space with exercise equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: NU’s campus-tour transcript identifies Eagle Fitness Center as a place where students and faculty can work out using its equipment.
cards.access_notes: The campus-tour page identifies student and faculty use; verify current eligibility and facility hours with NU before visiting.
